run: xSIM++ error rate and error-type breakdown, Creole to English
metric: xSIM++ error rate: the fraction of queries whose nearest passage is not a gold passage. This is the metric the method defines, so these numbers are comparable to other xSIM++ results. Chen et al., ACL 2023, https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12907
finding: Causality alternation is 4.4% of the distractors and causes about 51% of the errors for both morisien-embed and LaBSE, an enrichment of roughly 11.7x. Entity replacement is 88.2% of the pool and causes under a third of the errors, an enrichment of 0.3x. Both models handle a substituted entity and fail on a reversed causal direction, and they fail on it to the same degree. Number replacement sits between the two at about 2.5x.
consistency_check: morisien-embed 0.3143 against LaBSE 0.3072 puts LaBSE marginally ahead. That agrees with the nDCG@10 comparison in phase-a-xsim-eng.json, where the two are statistically indistinguishable out of domain, and it is computed by different code on a different metric.
caveats: Enrichment is computed against each rule's share of all 44,033 distractors, not against a per-query count. A query whose distractors are all of one type is weighted the same as any other, so this measures which rule the errors land on, not a per-rule error probability.

multilingual-e5-base retrieved 8 passages that are not released distractors at all. The other two models retrieved none, so almost every error is a released distractor rather than an unrelated passage.
One run per model. The encoders are deterministic here, but this has not been repeated.
